verdict.rationale: Jitsu Functions run on every incoming event and can filter, transform, or enrich it, and use the Fetch API to call third-party services. Combined with the webhook destination (Slack, Discord, any HTTP endpoint) and built-in failure alerts, this gives event-triggered actions. However, the 'rules' must be written as JavaScript/TypeScript code rather than defined in a rule or automation builder, and alerts only cover sync and batch job status. Missing for 10: declarative/no-code rule definition, documented conditional action triggers beyond custom code, independent hands-on corroboration of Functions-driven automation.
